nodes.name: Initial Electrodeposition of Micropyramids
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition was performed in a three-electrode set-up... Electrodeposition at 2 V for 120 s created micropyramids.

unit_operations.name: Electrodeposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Electrodeposition at 2 V for 120 s created micropyramids

nodes.source_text: Electrodeposition at 2 V for 120 s created micropyramids with an edge length of . 5 μm

nodes.name: Stacking Growth to Quaternary Structure
nodes.procedure: Electrodeposition at 4.5 V was performed to create the second-order building unit... Subsequent electrodeposition at 6.5 V for 10 s created the third-order nanodendrite... The fourth-order structure was created after electrodeposition at 10 V for 5 s.

unit_operations.name: Second-order growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Electrodeposition at 4.5 V ... evolved into starfruit-like microstructures after electrodeposition for 30 s

unit_operations.name: Third-order growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: Subsequent electrodeposition at 6.5 V for 10 s created the third-order nanodendrite

unit_operations.name: Fourth-order growth
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: The fourth-order structure was created after electrodeposition at 10 V for 5 s

nodes.source_text: Electrodeposition at 4.5 V ... 6.5 V for 10 s ... 10 V for 5 s, giving rise to the formation of quaternary microarchitectures

nodes.name: Gradually Decreasing Potential for Torpedoes
nodes.procedure: Microscale torpedoes prepared at 0.2 V/s potential-decreasing rate from 10 V to 2 V.
nodes.source_text: Microarchitectures prepared at 0.2 V s−1 potential-decreasing rate were composed of a microtorpedo standing on an arrowhead-like nanoparticle.

nodes.name: Chemical Conversion to Silver
nodes.procedure: The designed Ag7O8NO3 microstructures react with 50 mM NaBH4 aqueous solutions for 60 min, transforming into nanoporous silver microstructures.
nodes.source_text: react with 50 mM NaBH4 aqueous solutions for 60 min, transforming into nanoporous silver microstructures while keeping the morphology unchanged

nodes.name: Flattening Growth Mode
nodes.procedure: The concave surfaces of the starfruit-like structure were flattened when the potential was decreased from 4 V to 2 V. Electrodeposition at 2 V for 60 s evolved ternary microarchitectures into microcylinders with flat surfaces.
nodes.source_text: the concave surfaces of the starfruit-like structure were flattened when the potential was decreased from 4 V to 2 V ... evolved into microcylinders with flat surfaces after electrodeposition at 2 V for 60 s

nodes.name: Tower-like Stacking
nodes.procedure: Six potential-increasing processes created five stacking micropyramid caps. Each process involves increasing potential from 2 V to 10 V.
nodes.source_text: Six potential-increasing processes created five stacking micropyramid caps.

nodes.name: Conversion to Silver Chromate
nodes.procedure: Ag7O8NO3 microarchitectures were transformed into Ag2CrO4 after reacting with Cr(NO3)3 aqueous solutions. Leakage of Ag, N, and O created a hollow structure.
nodes.source_text: Ag7O8NO3 microarchitectures were transformed into Ag2CrO4 after reacting with Cr(NO3)3 aqueous solutions

nodes.description: SERS sensing performance for Rhodamine 6G (R6G) detection
nodes.source_text: Strong SERS signals of Rhodamine 6G (R6G) molecules from their aqueous solutions at a concentration of 1 nM were observed using the nanoporous silver microscale torpedoes as the SERS substrate... The detection limit of the nanoporous silver microscale torpedoes is as little as 1 pM.

In contrast, the SERS signals of R6G from 1 nM aqueous solutions were very weak when using the silver nanoparticle aggregate as the SERS substrate... no SERS signals of R6G molecules could be observed from their aqueous solutions at a concentration of 0.1 nM using the silver nanoparticle aggregate.

nodes.description: Catalytic propulsion performance in H2O2 (micromotor application)
nodes.source_text: The Ag7O8NO3 microscale torpedoes could vigorously react with clinically used H2O2 aqueous solutions (2.5 wt%) to continuously eject oxygen bubbles from their blunt end, pushing them to move spirally forward at an extremely fast speed (> 2 mm s−1).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman measurements revealed the formation of Ag(OH)2- species close to the anodic electrode during the initial growth stage.
nodes.evidence_snippet: giving rise to the formation of Ag(OH)2- close to the anodic electrode revealed by the in situ Raman measurements (Supplementary Fig. 3).

properties.description: Concentration-dependent Raman spectra showing signal decrease from 1 μM to 1 pM.

nodes.evidence_snippet: quasi-in situ scanning electron microscopy monitoring of the structural evolution when the potential was increased from 2 V ... further to 6 V (ternary microarchitecture).
